## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `--exclude` flag should take its default from `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE`, because the project's cli-flags rule requires an environment default for every newly added flag and CI sets options that way. This review found no other defect in the exclusion logic or its tests, which were read, not run.

## Changes
The pull request adds a repeatable `--exclude GLOB` flag to the archive CLI, which makes `collect` skip files whose base name matches any pattern and logs each skipped path. It also documents the flag in `docs/flags.md`, adds five tests, and adds a text fixture that no test references.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- cli/main.py:17 — correctness — Read the --exclude default from ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE — With `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE=*.log` set and no `--exclude` argument, the archive still includes `.log` files, because the flag hard-codes `default=[]`. This breaks the rule "Every command-line flag added under `cli/` from now on must also take its default from an `ARCHIVE_<NAME>` environment variable" (`.claude/skills/cli-flags/SKILL.md:11`). — CI jobs that set exclusions through the environment archive the files they meant to skip, with no error. — Fix: Decide how `ARCHIVE_EXCLUDE` separates multiple globs and whether `--exclude` adds to or replaces it (argparse `append` extends a non-empty default), then document it at `docs/flags.md:7`.
